pr_title: Optimize APF support for watch initialization to fix the pod startup time regression
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103578

As described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103578#issuecomment-879612196, this PR reduces the number of goroutines, pod startup time and API call latency back to from before the offending change preserving the functionality.

The regression was introduced in #102171

```release-note
NONE
```

/kind bug
/priority important-soon
/sig api-machinery
/sig scalability
pr_comments:
/milestone v1.22

@tkashem - this is now ready for (hopefully) final pass of review

This is a big change to something in the critical path... is there a pointer to the change that introduced the regression? Would it be helpful to structure this as a revert of that change, then a reimplementation of the functionality, rather than a single fix forward?

For 1.22, what is the risk of merging this vs just reverting the regression introduced in June?

> This is a big change to something in the critical path... is there a pointer to the change that introduced the regression? 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102171

> Would it be helpful to structure this as a revert of that change, then a reimplementation of the functionality, rather than a single fix forward?

Hmm - I'm not sure I see a big value from it - it would have to add visibly more files, the tests added back then are ensuring that this change also works as expected.

> For 1.22, what is the risk of merging this vs just reverting the regression introduced in June?

I think that the risk is low. The fact that this is on the critical path means that before the release we will have a very strong signal from it for the upcoming month. In case of problem, we can always go back and revert both if really needed.

OTOH - the gain from having this feature is very significant - it prevents large enough clusters under heavy load from entering  crashloops due to being overloaded after restart in multiple different situations.
@liggitt - I added one more test that now makes the code from this PR has 100% test coverage.

The coverage of the interesting part with this PR.

issue_context.title: Pod startup time latency increase around beginning of June
issue_context.body:
As visible in this graph:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10743879/124883115-4e50a900-dfd1-11eb-84d9-74b2e231de53.png)

pod-startup time in 5k-node tests increased around beginning of June (only 99% though).

It seems to be connected to "run-to-watch" phase.

We should investigate and see what we can do with this.

/sig scalability
/kind bug

@jkaniuk @jprzychodzen @marseel @kubernetes/sig-scalability

Once PR that merged around that time is P&F support for watch-initialitation:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102171

As a first step, we may want to confirm/reject if it's this PR and see if we aren't somehow misconfigured here.
I've briefly checked test-infra/perf-tests to see if we had any relevant changes around that time, but I don't see any. Most likely it's related to k/k changes.

Good news is that we can also see it regression in kubemark (although not as bad as in regular 5k tests):
http://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=kubemark-5000Nodes&metriccategoryname=E2E&metricname=LoadPodStartup&Metric=run_to_watch
But this can help us with finding root cause faster/cheaper.
